r: **Abul Hasan Yaminuddin Khusrau** (1253–1325); born at **Patiyali**, then **Etah** district (now **Kasganj**, UP)
**Tuti-i-Hind** ("Parrot of India") – he called himself so
Chiefly **Alauddin Khalji's** court poet; **poet laureate** with a state pension under **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq**
Served about **seven** Sultans (Kaiqubad, Jalaluddin, Alauddin, Mubarak Shah, Ghiyasuddin …)
Disciple of Chishti saint **Nizamuddin Auliya** (who also lived under seven or more Sultans) – a **Sufi**, not a Bhakti figure
Savant of both **Persian and Hindavi (Hindi)**; **first to use Urdu** (emerging Hindavi/Rekhta) for poetry; **Father of Khari Boli**; his riddles and verses in Hindavi grew into Rekhta/Urdu
Founder of **Sabak-i-Hindi** (Indian style); **first Persian poet to depict the Indian environment**; said "Na Lafze Hindiwast az Farsi Kam"
"Every pearl in the royal crown is the crystallised drop of blood fallen from the tearful eyes of the poor peasant"
Credited to **Amir Khusrau**; combines the Indian **veena** with the Iranian **tambura** – the classic example of **Hindu-Muslim harmony** in instruments
Also credited to **Amir Khusrau** (developed from the pakhawaj)
Earliest Persian treatise on Indian music
**Alauddin's** early years and conquests, incl. the Deccan
Meeting of **Bughra Khan** and his son **Kaiqubad**
Romance of **Deval Rani – Khizr Khan** (Alauddin's son)

3.x: All six works are by **Amir Khusrau** (the Tughluqnama is not Ibn Battuta's).

r: **Qazi of Delhi** under **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**; sent as **envoy to China** (1342)
Travelogue in **Arabic** – throws light on **MBT's reign**
Arabicised, mixed with Turkish – **official language** of the Sultanate
Grew in camps and bazaars; Deccan form = **Dakhni**
The late Prakrit dialects – **early forms of modern Indian languages**
Lived through seven or more reigns but **never visited the court**
Refused to meet him: "My house has **two doors** – if the Sultan enters by one, I will leave by the other."
Tried to meet him through Khusrau; the saint left for **Ajodhan**
His conversations (malfuzat), recorded by **Amir Hasan Sijzi**
Malik Muhammad Jayasi (Urdu version by **Ghulam Ali**, court poet of **Tana Shah**)
**Abdullah Qutb Shah** and **Abul Hasan Tana Shah**

Bijapur, **Ibrahim Adil Shah II**; calls Telangana "Tilang"; fall of Warangal 1323
